notes:
Inbound: trial signup via website (marquee support automation template). Early discovery call 2026-03-03 (FF id ff_20260303_0921).

Key contact: Maya Ortiz (Head of Ops) + engineering lead Tom Bender.

CRM-style bullets from notes: 
- Wants a light-touch hosted integration first (self-serve).
- Primary need: condense agent threads into 2-3 line summaries + auto-suggest resolution steps.
- Secondary: tool-calling to run ticket state changes (e.g., /add-tag, /escalate) from chat assistant -> must support structured output for ticketing API.
- Latency tolerance: < 400ms p50 for assistant suggestions, < 800ms p95. Throughput: small peaks (~20 rps) during weekday mornings.
- Cost sensitivity: prefers predictable per-month budget vs per-token spikes; asking about cost caps and alerts.
- Security ask: SOC2 report + SSO (SAML) and audit logging (retention 1 year). Data residency not strict today (US preferred).
- Model preferences: start with open Llama family / quantized for cost; willing to evaluate Redwood-curated models. Fallback: lower-cost variant if latency spikes.
- POC plan: 2-week self-serve trial with sample ticket dataset; measure summary accuracy (recall/precision on flagged issues) and false positive rate for auto-escalation.

Quotes/phrases from call: 
- "We need something that our agents trust — short, accurate summaries, not hallucinations." — Maya.
- "If we can try without legal hoops, we'll spin it into product quickly." — Tom.

Stubs/links referenced in notes: pricing deck (drive link above), sample dataset uploaded to shared folder, Jira ticket RDW-1120 tracking SOC2 artifact request.
